_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); revenue, margin, expense and receivables signals with Google's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Alphabet is a collection of businesses — the largest of which is Google.' 'We generate a significant portion of our revenues from advertising.' 'We face intense competition.' 'Our operating results have fluctuated, and may in the future fluctuate, as a result of a number of factors, many outside of our control, including the cyclicality and seasonality in our business and geopolitical events.' 'In addition, expenditures by advertisers tend to correlate with overall economic conditions.' (FY2022 10-K); CYCLICAL: the 10-K says so of its own business ('the cyclicality and seasonality in our business'), the BKR, CAT and NVDA reading, not an industry's words; CLOUD (live from 2012-10-30) is scoped to public cloud displacing on-premise IT, and this 10-K names the cloud as Google's own business ('Within Google Cloud, we devote significant resources to develop and deploy our enterprise-ready cloud services, including Google Cloud Platform and Google Workspace') and enterprise cloud providers as its competitors, so it is out of scope (the AVGO FY2012 and NVDA reading); ECOMMERCE (from 2015-01-01), STREAMING (from 2015-08-04) and ENERGY_TRANSITION (from 2015-12-12) are scoped to physical retail, linear TV and pay-TV bundles, and fossil fuels; EV (from 2020-01-01) to combustion-engine vehicles and their suppliers; CRYPTO (from 2020-10-21) to payment networks, banks and exchanges; GENAI (live from 2022-11-30) is scoped to generative AI substituting core products, search among them, but a theme joins the watch list only from a company filing that names it as a competitive risk (the PEP GLP1 rule, as for MSFT), and this 10-K names AI only as Google's own products, their challenges and their effect on its own monetization ('new and evolving products and services, including those that use AI, require significant investment and raise ethical, technological, legal, regulatory, and other challenges, which may negatively affect our brands and demand for our products and services.' 'We also may develop new products incorporating AI innovations that could affect our monetization trends.'), so the watch list is empty; the competition named is a competitive field, not a theme, and stays here (the PEP obesity rule)

BEAR.desc: EPS -35.4%/yr (worst year FY13-FY22, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +7.4%/yr (Q2 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +18.8%/yr (FY13-FY22 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +65.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY13-FY22, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: GOOG (retrospective, 2023-09-01) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B 2.15x (70.0% downside to Bear $41.04 / +32.6% upside to Bull $181.33) | Adj composite 1.75 vs market 2.59: gap -0.84 [OVERVALUED] | +50% above the EPP floor $91.20 (20x FY23E $4.56) | Conservative 2-yr case: -7.4% total (-3.7%/yr) | At 30.0x FY23E the 15% hurdle price $180.92 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +7.1% YoY in Q2 2023, forward revenues +7.1% (Q2 2023 revenue growth (no Q3 2023 guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
